--- title: Data Report --- The project is based on a single raw dataset downloaded from the link provided on moodle (´https://moodle.zhaw.ch/pluginfile.php/2585021/mod_page/content/2/traveldata-export.xlsx´). It contains detailed corporate travel records from the year 2017 to the beginning of 2026. The dataset includes multimodal travel information (flights, trains, buses, rental cars) and associated emissions, costs, and metadata. ## Raw data ### Overview Raw Datasets : Overview of raw datasets used in the project. {#tbl-raw-overview} | Name | Quelle          | Storage location | |:-----------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | traveldata-export.xlsx | Internal corporate travel logs (flights, trains, buses, rental cars) | In this project:
ad24-2-fancyproject/traveldata-export.xlsx

On PODSV FS26 Moodle: https://moodle.zhaw.ch/pluginfile.php/2585021/mod_page/content/2/traveldata-export.xlsx | ### Details Dataset 1 This dataset contains individual travel records for employees and guests, covering:
- Travel mode (flight, train, bus, rental car)
- Departure and arrival locations (IATA codes, cities, countries, continents, coordinates)
- Flight‑specific attributes (aircraft type, haul type, travel class, flight number)
- Emissions data (CO₂e with RFI 2.0 and RFI 2.7)
- Distance travelled (km)
- Business metadata (business unit, subunit, travel purpose)
- Cost information (CHF)
- Availability of train alternatives
Each row represents a single travel segment. The data originates from the company’s internal travel management system, which aggregates bookings from airlines, rail operators, bus companies, and rental car providers.
The dataset was exported from the corporate travel system as an Excel file. Contains personal‑related business travel data, but no direct personal identifiers. Use is restricted to internal analytics and sustainability reporting.
Category: Internal, business‑relevant
Sensitivity: Medium (travel patterns may indirectly identify individuals) Independent variables: travel mode, distance, business unit, travel purpose, geography
Dependent variables: CO₂e emissions, cost

**Correlation matrix heatmap of categorical variables** ::: {#cell-corr-c .cell message='false' execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code code-fold="true"} from scipy.stats import chi2_contingency def cramers_v(x, y): """Compute Cramér's V for two categorical variables.""" confusion_matrix = pd.crosstab(x, y) chi2 = chi2_contingency(confusion_matrix)[0] n = confusion_matrix.sum().sum() r, k = confusion_matrix.shape return np.sqrt(chi2 / (n * (min(r - 1, k - 1)))) cat_cols = raw_df.select_dtypes(include=["object", "category"]).columns cramers_matrix = pd.DataFrame( np.zeros((len(cat_cols), len(cat_cols))), index=cat_cols, columns=cat_cols ) for col1 in cat_cols: for col2 in cat_cols: cramers_matrix.loc[col1, col2] = cramers_v(raw_df[col1], raw_df[col2]) plt.figure(figsize=(12, 10)) sns.heatmap( cramers_matrix, annot=True, cmap="coolwarm", vmin=0, vmax=1, square=True ) plt.title("Cramér's V Heatmap for Categorical Variables") plt.tight_layout() plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Correlation matrix heatmap of categoricals](data_report_files/figure-html/corr-c-output-1.png){#corr-c width=1061 height=962} ::: ::: Figures can be referenced like @corr-c. ___ The results the exploratory data analysis should be summarised here (code and full output in the `eda` subfolder) and the implications for the subsequent data pre-processing, visualization design and implementation steps should be discussed.
